name: Summarization
description: Summarize memory content for use as a description in a vector database and semantic search — seeded from MemoryAPI's memory-summary prompt. Scored via LLM rubric (conciseness, faithfulness, coverage), not deterministic checks.
seedPromptContent:
Summarize the following memory content for use as an effective content description in a vector database and semantic search. Return only the summary, with no preamble or explanation.

The memory content to summarize will be given in the next message.

starterTestCases.userMessage: Meeting notes from the Q3 planning session: we agreed to prioritize the mobile redesign over the API v2 migration this quarter, since customer support tickets show the mobile UI is the top complaint. Sarah will own the redesign spec, due in two weeks. The API migration is pushed to Q4. starterTestCases.referenceAnswer: Q3 planning prioritized the mobile redesign, owned by Sarah with a specification due in two weeks; API v2 moved to Q4, and QA contractor hiring awaits budget confirmation.

starterTestCases.userMessage: I've been reading about transformer architectures and how attention mechanisms let models weigh the relevance of different tokens in a sequence, rather than processing everything sequentially like RNNs did. The key insight is self-attention: every token can directly attend to every other token in a single layer, which is why transformers parallelize so much better on GPUs than recurrent models ever did.
starterTestCases.description: Technical learning note explaining a concept
starterTestCases.referenceAnswer: Transformers use self-attention so each token can weigh every other token within a layer, enabling better GPU parallelism than sequential recurrent models.
requiredFacts: transformers parallelize better than recurrent models
forbiddenClaims: RNNs process every token in parallel

starterTestCases.userMessage: Idea for a side project: a browser extension that automatically summarizes long Slack threads into a 3-bullet TL;DR using a local LLM, so you don't have to scroll through 200 messages to catch up after being out for a day. Could start with just Slack, but Discord and Teams would be natural extensions later.
starterTestCases.description: Project idea with a core concept and possible extensions
starterTestCases.referenceAnswer: A proposed browser extension would use a local LLM to summarize long Slack threads into three bullets, with possible later support for Discord and Teams.
requiredFacts: Discord and Teams are possible extensions
